title: Holding Limit for Insurer Program Agreements
content:
**Clause.** An insurer account holds at most one program agreement under the Insurer Program Agreements at a time; a change of tier is a renewal or re-rating of the same agreement, never a second agreement. Only an insurer account (an account whose customer type on its customer record is insurer) may hold one. No agreement other than a terminated one exists for the insurer.

The limit is 1 agreement per insurer account, and it is the same in every tier:

| Agreement tier | Program agreements one insurer account may hold at once |
|---|---|
| Network Referral Agreement | 1 |
| Select Direct Repair Agreement | 1 |
| Preferred Direct Repair Agreement | 1 |
| Premier Direct Repair Agreement | 1 |
| Managed Repair Program Agreement | 1 |
| Enterprise Master Services Agreement | 1 |

## When the clause is applied

The clause governs the proposal of a program agreement with an insurer. A proposal opens an agreement for the insurer account and records the agreement reference, the insurer account, the agreement tier, the date proposed and the assignments per year the insurer commits.

The condition for a proposal is that **no agreement other than a terminated one exists for the insurer**. It is read from the company's agreement records for that same insurer account, before the proposal is made; it is not established by what a caller says about the insurer's agreements. Every agreement of the insurer account counts, whatever its tier.

## Statuses of the insurer's existing agreements

| Existing agreements of the insurer account | Condition met |
|---|---|
| None | Yes |
| Only terminated ones | Yes |
| At least one proposed | No |
| At least one active | No |
| At least one under review | No |
| At least one suspended | No |

## Cases (hypothetical accounts)

- An insurer account whose only agreement was terminated may be the subject of a new proposal: the terminated agreement does not count.
- An insurer account holding an active Select Direct Repair Agreement that is to move to the Preferred tier does not receive a second agreement: the change of tier is a renewal or re-rating of the same agreement.
- An insurer account whose agreement is suspended still holds that agreement, and the condition for a new proposal is not met.
- An account whose customer type is not insurer, such as a fleet account, may not hold a program agreement.
